title: Biotechnology Market Companies 2027 Analysis: Amgen, Gilead, Regeneron, Vertex and Moderna Post Strong 2026 Results as Billion-Dollar Deals Reshape a Market Headed for USD 6.34 Trillion by 2035
author: Precedence Research
description: The global biotechnology market, valued at USD 2.02 trillion in 2026, is projected to reach USD 6.34 trillion by 2035 at a 13.61% CAGR. Leading biotech companies including Amgen, Gilead, Regeneron, Vertex, and Moderna reported strong Q3 2026 results with revenue growth ranging from 8% to 36%. The sector experienced record dealmaking activity with major acquisitions totaling tens of billions of dollars, driven by patent expiries, strong cash flows, and strategic pipeline expansion in oncology, immunology, and advanced therapies.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Q3 2026 revenue grew 8% to USD 10.4B with strong growth in newer products (Repatha +37%, Evenity +39%, Tezspire +43%, Imdelltra +128%). Raised full-year guidance and increased R&D spending by 11%, demonstrating confidence in pipeline and ability to offset biosimilar competition on older drugs.

Q3 2026 product sales grew 13% to USD 8.3B with HIV revenue up 18%. Announced four acquisitions worth USD 12.7B upfront, raised full-year product sales guidance to USD 31.0-31.3B, and demonstrated aggressive pipeline expansion strategy in cell therapy and immunology.

Q3 2026 revenue climbed 36% to USD 5.1B, the strongest growth among peers, driven by Dupixent sales of USD 6.5B (+35%) and EYLEA HD (+62%). Expanded Sanofi collaboration with USD 1B upfront and up to USD 7B in milestones, and guides to over USD 6B in annual R&D.

Q3 2026 revenue grew 12% to USD 3.44B with strong cystic fibrosis franchise performance. Gene-edited Casgevy earned USD 99M (nearly 6x year-over-year growth), raised full-year guidance to USD 13.15-13.25B, and acquired Crinetics to expand pipeline.

Q3 2026 revenue rose 29% to USD 1.3B. mRNA flu vaccine approved by FDA in August 2026, positive Phase 3 results for cancer vaccine (intismeran autogene) with 42% risk reduction in melanoma recurrence, and raised full-year revenue growth guidance to 15-25%.

Q3 2026 revenue EUR 1.29B with guidance of EUR 1.7-1.9B for full year. Running seven pivotal trials of pumitamig (oncology bispecific with BMS) but facing headwind from declining COVID-19 vaccine revenue. Pivoting to oncology represents strategic shift but near-term revenue pressure.

Partnering with BioNTech on pumitamig (PD-L1×VEGF-A bispecific) with seven pivotal oncology trials underway. Collaboration indicates strategic focus on next-generation oncology formats, but limited specific financial impact disclosed in this article.

Partnering with BioNTech on pumitamig (PD-L1×VEGF-A bispecific) with seven pivotal oncology trials underway. Collaboration indicates strategic focus on next-generation oncology formats, but limited specific financial impact disclosed in this article.

Agreed to acquire Nuvalent for USD 10.6B to gain lung cancer targeted therapy assets. Demonstrates strategic investment in oncology, one of the largest destinations for biotech investment, and commitment to pipeline expansion ahead of patent expiries.

Announced approximately USD 10.8B in 2026 deals including Centessa acquisition, focusing on neuroscience and other therapeutic areas. Active dealmaking demonstrates commitment to pipeline expansion and positioning for long-term growth.

Acquired Terns Pharmaceuticals for approximately USD 6.7B to gain chronic myeloid leukemia assets. Also reported positive Phase 3 results with Moderna for intismeran autogene cancer vaccine. Strategic investments in oncology align with market growth drivers.

Acquired Apellis Pharmaceuticals for USD 5.6B upfront to gain immunology and rare disease assets. Demonstrates commitment to expanding portfolio in high-growth therapeutic areas and securing late-stage assets.

Announced collaboration with Innovent for up to USD 10.5B in ADCs and multi-specific antibodies. Partnership indicates strategic focus on next-generation modalities but represents collaboration rather than full acquisition, limiting direct revenue impact.

Expanded long-acting antibody collaboration with Regeneron in October 2026 with USD 1B upfront and up to USD 7B in milestones, building on Dupixent's success. Partnership extension demonstrates confidence in immunology franchise and access to next-generation antibody technology.

title: Should You Invest in the VanEck Biotech ETF (BBH)?
author: Na
description: The VanEck Biotech ETF (BBH) is a passively managed fund tracking the MVIS US Listed Biotech 25 Index with $521.91 million in assets and a low 0.35% expense ratio. The fund has delivered strong year-to-date returns of 31.47% but carries higher risk with a beta of 0.70 and concentrated exposure through its top 10 holdings representing 73.82% of assets. BBH holds a Zacks ETF Rank of 2 (Buy), though investors should consider alternatives like XBI and IBB.

title: AstraZeneca Secures US, EU Nod for New Myasthenia Gravis Drug Klygefa
author: Zacks.Com
description: AstraZeneca received FDA and EU regulatory approvals for Klygefa (gefurulimab), a complement C5 inhibitor for treating adults with AChR-positive generalized myasthenia gravis. The once-weekly, self-administered subcutaneous therapy showed significant improvements in daily activities versus placebo in Phase III trials. While the convenient dosing offers differentiation from AstraZeneca's existing IV therapies (Soliris and Ultomiris), Klygefa faces cannibalization risks and competition from other complement C5 inhibitors and alternative mechanism drugs.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Secured regulatory approvals in major markets (US and EU) for a new drug with differentiated once-weekly self-administration, expanding its gMG treatment portfolio and offering convenience advantages over existing therapies.
Faces increased competition from Klygefa's once-weekly dosing advantage over its Zilbrysq (once-daily) and maintains competitive position with alternative mechanisms like Rystiggo.

title: Anti-Obesity Drugs Market Companies Analysis 2027: Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk Lead as Pfizer, Roche and Amgen Invest Billions to Challenge Them in a Market Headed for USD 64.96 Billion by 2035
author: Precedence Research
description: The global anti-obesity drugs market is valued at USD 8.96 billion in 2026 and projected to reach USD 64.96 billion by 2035 at a 24.71% CAGR. Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk dominate with strong Q3 2026 results, while Pfizer, Roche, and Amgen are investing billions to compete. Key trends include oral GLP-1 formulations, higher efficacy rates (>20% weight loss), and significant manufacturing capacity investments.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Market leader with strong Q3 2026 revenue growth of 39% to USD 24.4B. Mounjaro and Zepbound combined generated USD 16.1B. Foundayo oral GLP-1 approved and generating sales. Retatrutide in Phase 3 showing 22.6% weight loss. USD 50B investment in U.S. manufacturing demonstrates confidence and competitive positioning.

No. 2 market leader with obesity sales rising 22% to DKK 26.1B. Wegovy pill launched in U.S. January 2026 with strong uptake (8M+ prescriptions). CagriSema filed with FDA showing 22.7% weight loss. Raised 2026 outlook and investing DKK 50B in capital expenditure to defend market share.

Re-entering obesity market through USD 10B acquisition of Metsera completed November 2025 after ending its own oral GLP-1 program. Acquisition provides access to long-acting injectable pipeline but represents a catch-up strategy rather than organic innovation leadership.

Entered obesity market with MariTide, a long-acting GLP-1 antibody-peptide. Phase 3 trials launched in 2026 targeting less frequent dosing. Early-stage competitor with potential differentiation but not yet proven in market.

Partnering for amylin-based therapies through USD 5.3B collaboration with Zealand Pharma (May 2025). Building obesity franchise but remains a challenger rather than leader. Strategy focuses on differentiated mechanisms rather than market dominance.

title: Which Healthcare ETF Is the Better Buy: State Street’s Pharma Fund XPH or iShares’ Biotech Fund IBB?
author: Sara Appino
description: The article compares two healthcare ETFs: State Street's XPH (Pharmaceuticals) and iShares' IBB (Biotechnology). XPH charges lower fees (0.35% vs 0.44%), offers higher dividend yield (0.4% vs 0.2%), and focuses on smaller pharmaceutical companies that are acquisition targets. IBB is significantly larger with $11.3B in assets under management and holds 243 established biotech firms. The analyst recommends XPH for long-term investors due to the pharmaceutical industry's active M&A activity and smaller companies' takeover potential.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recommended as the better buy due to lower expense ratio (0.35%), higher dividend yield (0.4%), and strategic positioning to benefit from pharmaceutical industry M&A activity. The fund's focus on smaller companies that are acquisition targets provides upside potential.
